Subject: KCK-4471 – Vantorre CX-10 review

We bought the refurbished Vantorre CX-10 (listing KCK-4471) for $14,800 inc GST. It was delivered and commissioned on 14 September 2026 with a six-month parts and labour warranty. We had repeated E34 steam generator low water level faults from the start.

Service report SR-1190 (22/09): E34 logged nine times since 14/09; water level sensor replaced; inlet pressure 320 kPa. SR-1236 (06/10): steam generator found heavily scaled, descaled and flushed; core probe recalibrated. Before that, on 03/10, I reported E34 four times that week and a probe error: the oven read 63°C in a lamb shoulder while a Thermapen read 70°C, twice with the same result.

On Saturday 24 October at 6.10pm the unit locked out on E34 again with a full book of 60 covers. We finished the lamb on the stove and deck oven, 86'd the pork belly and absorbed the cost.

On 27/10 Kelsall attended again, found further scale, and invoiced the callout at $280 + GST ($308 inc GST), saying it was a site water issue and not warranty.

Technical point: our water supplier confirmed Fitzroy supply averages about 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which is soft. The unit had only been on our water three weeks when heavy scale was first found. A combi should not scale up in three weeks on 15 mg/L water; that points to scale being present before delivery or coming from another cause in the unit. That matters for any buyer.

Ask for the steam generator inspection/descale record and the warranty position in writing before buying a refurbished combi. Dion was responsive throughout.

reasons: It says the callout was invoiced, but Brett said it would be invoiced.
